notes:
Foundation release: BrokerAdapter abstraction goes live in production.

### What changed for users

Behaviour is byte-identical to v1.0.23 on a happy path — if you're on the default MT5 broker, you won't notice anything different. What changed is the plumbing underneath: the engine now boots through the BrokerAdapter abstraction instead of calling MetaTrader5 directly. This is the foundation for cTrader / DXTrade / TradeLocker support that v1.0.25+ will build out.

### Why this is a small ship

The original v1.0.24 brief planned a 600-call-site migration. Recon turned up two big surprises: (1) the brokers/ adapter scaffold + a 580-line MT5Adapter were already built in a prior initiative, and (2) the actual mt5.* call-site count is 114, all in engine.py — server.py and database.py have zero. What was missing was the activation: the engine's boot path called mt5_connect() directly instead of broker_connect(), so the adapter was never set in production. v1.0.24 flips that switch.

### Migration progress

2/114 mt5.* call sites migrated as a pattern demo (account_info paths in _safe_state). Of the remaining 112 sites, ~70 are realistically migratable read paths; ~44 are MT5 implementation glue (mt5_connect itself, AlreadyLoggedIn detection, reconnect supervisor) that won't migrate because they ARE the MT5 broker. Order-placement migration (mt5.order_send → adapter) is deferred to v1.0.25 — those touch real money and deserve dedicated focus + live-MT5 verification.

### What v1.0.25 unlocks

With the adapter live in production, v1.0.25 can build out CTraderAdapter (Open API REST + WebSocket OAuth), add a 'Pick your platform' onboarding wizard that writes cfg.broker_platform, and plug in the TradingView Cloudflare Worker relay as a separate signal source. None of that touches engine call sites.
